learningObjective: Move data with AzCopy (copy, sync, copies between accounts) and Storage Explorer, using the right kind of sign-in, and fix failed transfers.
engineer: Signing in to AzCopy: azcopy login (interactive, device code, managed identity or service principal) needs an Entra data role such as Storage Blob Data Contributor. Owner or Contributor alone is not enough. Or add a SAS to each URL instead.

AzCopy commands: azcopy copy, a one-time copy (add --recursive for folders); azcopy sync, copies only new or changed files, by last-modified time (add --delete-destination=true to also delete what you deleted); azcopy make, creates a container or share; azcopy remove; azcopy list; azcopy jobs list, resume and show, to finish a failed transfer.
Copying between accounts: happens inside Azure (server-side copy), so the data never passes through your computer.
Handy flags: --include-pattern; --exclude-pattern; --overwrite; --put-md5, saves a checksum; --cap-mbps, limits speed; --block-blob-tier, sets the tier on upload.
Storage Explorer sign-in options: Entra ID (a subscription or one resource); account name and key; SAS URL; connection string. It can also connect to Azurite, the local emulator.
What Storage Explorer can do: manage access policies; create SAS; change tiers; undelete soft-deleted blobs; work with Data Lake permissions (ACLs).
Firewall: storage firewall rules apply to both tools. Your IP or network must be allowed.

example.title: Copying a reports folder every night
body: A Windows server runs a scheduled task. First azcopy login --identity, which signs in as the VM's managed identity (it has Storage Blob Data Contributor). Then azcopy sync C:\reports https://stcontoso.blob.core.windows.net/reports --recursive --delete-destination=true.
After a network cut, azcopy jobs resume finishes the job without uploading the finished files again.

architectureDecisions: Scheduled jobs sign in as a managed identity: use azcopy login, and don't put SAS tokens in scripts.
Huge moves over slow links: use Data Box for many terabytes.

misconceptions.myth: An Owner can upload after azcopy login.
misconceptions.reality: No. A data role such as Storage Blob Data Contributor is needed.

misconceptions.myth: Copying between two accounts downloads the data to your PC first.
misconceptions.reality: No. AzCopy copies directly between accounts, inside Azure.

comparisons.difference: A physical device Microsoft ships to you, for very large data or slow internet. AzCopy copies over the network.
Keeps Windows Servers and Azure Files in sync all the time, with cloud tiering. AzCopy runs one-off or scheduled copies.

comparisons.service: AWS CLI s3 cp / s3 sync

troubleshooting.symptom: AzCopy returns 403 AuthorizationPermissionMismatch after azcopy login.
troubleshooting.cause: The identity has no Storage Blob Data role.
troubleshooting.fix: Give Storage Blob Data Contributor and wait a few minutes.

troubleshooting.cause: The storage firewall blocks your IP.
troubleshooting.fix: Add your IP, or use an allowed network.
Run azcopy jobs resume <job-id> (with the same SAS if you used one).

troubleshooting.cause: Last-modified times are different (for example after a restore).
troubleshooting.fix: Use --compare-hash where supported, or accept one full sync.

configuration.limits: sync compares last-modified times (or hashes, if you ask)
Firewall rules apply to your computer
configuration.permissions: Storage Blob Data Contributor (or Reader, for downloads) with azcopy login
Or a SAS with the permissions needed
configuration.prerequisites: AzCopy v10 or Storage Explorer installed
Network access to the storage endpoints
